dedupe_keys.name: york automatic cycle counters city of york council

description: The City of York Council publishes counts from automatic cycle counters installed at over forty sites in the city on York Open Data. Inductive loops in the cycleway or carriageway record cycles passing over them by direction and by hour of the day, and the council uses the data to monitor scheme implementation and trends in cycling to judge the effect of policy measures. Coverage: York, England, with one CSV file per calendar year from 2003 to 2021 and a site reference file giving each counter's location and direction; a separate dataset maps the counter locations. Format and access: CSV downloads from the CKAN portal. Licence and cost: free under the Open Government Licence v3.0. Caveats: the portal's newest annual file was added in November 2022, so later years are not published there, and loop counters can miss or double count riders when they ride outside the loop. The hourly directional counts can be used to calibrate cycling demand and network flow models and to check simulated responses to new cycle schemes. It relates to the Department for Transport road traffic counts, which the page points to for other York cycling counts, and to Melbourne's pedestrian counting system in the catalogue.
